_doc: pvscore 5.1 r1 view / body layer (tools/v51_r1/view_score.py loads this file; view_thresholds.json is the unchanged r0 file). Written 10-18 BEFORE any r1 score of a real model (astra / sol56 / gpt-6.1-sol) was computed. Values come from first principles, GT-only statistics of the five pilot checklists (data/v51_pilot, checklist + scene_frames only), the fake dump and the controls; nothing is tuned toward a model ranking. Every key of the r0 file is kept with its r0 value; new or changed rules are marked r1 and explained in data/v51_r1/notes_view.md. A later change gets a new file name. Amendment (10-18, after the first r1 run, before any control was judged): presence.continuation_neg_t_max_s, a scope fix raised by the checklist agent (scope_r1.json continuation rule: only content the model was given is scored); not derived from any score. The first-run output is kept as data/v51_r1/view_scores_r1_prescope.json.
_height_doc: unchanged: |log(model / GT height_frac)|: full at log 1.4, zero at log 2.5
_speed_doc: unchanged values; r1 reads only still (still_full / still_zero) and moving (move_zero / move_full) - the two ramps are complementary (still + moving = 1 for any speed). walk_* / run_* are kept for the record and no longer read

size_trend._doc: r1 uncertainty band. Model ratio r = last / first height_frac over the run, x = log r. approach = ramp(x: log 1.15 -> 0, log 1.30 -> 1), recede = the same ramp on -x (1/1.15 = 0.87 -> 0, 1/1.30 = 0.77 -> 1), same = 1 - approach - recede (1 inside |x| <= log 1.15, 0 beyond log 1.30): the three answers are complementary, so a ratio between 1.15 and 1.30 is half credited instead of being forced into a class. 1.15 = the layer's other ratio margins (depth_ratio, path.cam_ratio); 1.30 = the checklist's own approach_ratio, so a GT approach / recede fact (GT ratio >= 1.30 / <= 0.77) asks for the same strength in the model. A GT 'same' fact is scored only when its GT ratio is within 1.15 (|log r_gt| <= log 1.15): a GT 'same' of 0.80 or 1.20 sits inside the band itself (GT pilot: 5 of 30 'same' facts) and is parked

_screen_dir_min_dx_doc: r0 only (screen-x displacement); r1 reads every lateral direction fact by definition A (segment_dir) and no longer reads this

segment_dir.note: as pvscore 5.0.10 seg_dir_away_deg / seg_dir_static_h; r1 applies it to every lateral direction fact (lateral below)

lateral._doc: r1: every lateral direction fact (single-label screen_dir of the shot, GT r1 screen_dir segments, and locomotion_segment screen directions) is read by definition A = pvscore 5.0.10 camera._segment_dir: trim trim x duration at both ends, body-centre displacement between the first and last present body rows (x, y in model units x xy_scale = body heights), projected on the camera's horizontal right (cam_r) / forward (cam_f) axes at the row nearest the middle; |d| < segment_dir.static_h -> static, heading within away_deg of forward -> away, of backward -> toward, else left_to_right / right_to_left by the sign on cam_r. min_dur_s 0.5: after the 10% trims 0.4 s remain, at least one model grid time (0.25 s step) and up to two; shorter facts are parked; a fact whose trimmed window holds fewer than 2 present body rows scores 0 (the model cannot be read there; detail 'why'). [Doc corrected 10-18 after the first run: the earlier text said '>= 2 grid times', which is wrong for a 0.4 s window; the value is unchanged.] GT label of a locomotion_segment (V2 run): the cell-column direction (screen_dir) only when the GT shot's camera move is in static_cam_moves (a still camera: screen motion = lateral heading); otherwise the GT heading label gt_screen_dir (shot label or the overlapping GT r1 segment); otherwise parked (a cell change under a pan / follow / unknown move is not a heading). Runs of a type in park_types are parked (no heading). Not read on the video side (no camera pose).

locomotion._doc: r1: only informative locomotion facts are read. still vs moving (walk / run / move / drive / ride / skate collapse to moving, scored by the complementary speed ramps speed_h.still_* / move_*; the walk-vs-run speed bands are parked: V2's walk / run word follows the action verb, not a speed the model can be held to); jump / land (any airborne row in the window, as r0); climb (r1: the base height rises >= climb.rise_h body heights between two rows, earlier lower, inside the run +- climb.pad_s; r0 took the range, so a drop also passed; values = temporal_thresholds.json climb = path.up_down_h); fall (r1, new: inside the run +- fall.pad_s the body extent (top_h - base_h) falls from >= extent_hi to <= extent_lo within within_s, or the base drops >= drop_h; values = temporal_thresholds.json fall = the 5.0.9 fall detector, so the two layers share one definition). roll / slide and other words are parked (a roll / skid has no reliable sign in the body series). R = best constant answer over {still, moving}: a constant body that is never airborne and never changes height scores 0 on every event fact; an 'always airborne' answer is not a candidate (it would also fail posture and the no_air control; noted as an open point)

presence._continuation_doc: r1 amendment (10-18, after the first r1 run): on items with gt.image_kind == continuation (021, 024) the model is given frame 1 and the prompt only (tools/v51_r1/scope_r1.json continuation, f1_s 0.05). A derived 'must NOT be in view' fact after frame 1 is almost never stated in the prompt (021 K02 names only P01, not that P02 is out of view), so under the registered scope rule it is not_applicable: negatives (a) are kept only at V2 times <= 0.05 s (= scope_r1.json f1_s). The absent halves (b) of enter / exit / occluded entries are kept: those entries already passed the scope filter. Presence on a continuation item then has few negatives and is flagged low-information by min_class_n: a prompt that never says who is out of view cannot tell an 'everyone always visible' answer from a correct one.
presence._doc: r1: presence is scored by balanced accuracy over positives (screen_track rows, in_frame, landmark_present, the visible-now half of enter_frame / exit_frame / occluded) and GT-derived negatives: (a) at every V2 row time of a shot (scene_frames samples), each cast subject (P / V id with a screen_track row anywhere in the item) that has no screen_track row in that shot within row_match_s must NOT be in view, provided its nearest row of that shot is >= neg_margin_s away (V2 rows are ~1 s apart; 0.75 s covers the time-map tolerance 0.13 + 0.3 s plus V2's own timing error) and the time is not inside a freeze frame (annot/video_freeze_20261017.json); (b) the absent-in-window half of enter_frame / exit_frame / occluded (r0 tested it jointly with the visible half). BA = (TPR + TNR) / 2, R = 0.5 for any constant or content-free answer. A block with fewer than min_class_n facts in either class is flagged low-information (BA of < 5 facts is too noisy).

position_chance._doc: r1: R = the best score a single constant cell answer gets on the block's present facts, with each cell pooled with its left-right mirror (a content-free answer can know that subjects sit near the centre, not on which side): R = max_c mean_f (s(g_f, c) + s(g_f, mirror c)) / 2. GT-only on the pilot it equals the unpooled best constant (centre wins on all 5 items: 0.62-0.73) and exceeds the uniform-grid R of r0 (0.46-0.47). The uniform and pi-random (a guess drawn from the GT cell distribution) values are reported as diagnostics.

low_info._doc: r1: a block whose GT-only chance R_gt (the block's R computed from the GT facts alone, all facts) is >= r_max is flagged informative = false (score kept as computed): above 0.75 a constant answer already gets 75% and (P - R) / (1 - R) amplifies every fact's noise >= 4x. Pairwise blocks (screen_order, depth_order) have a model-side permutation R and are not flagged by this rule; presence is flagged by min_class_n instead (its R is 0.5 by construction).

chance.pairwise: unchanged: permute (box, centre, depth) among the model's non-surface elements of each frame, recheck the same facts; R = mean over perms
chance.height: unchanged: model height_frac log-uniform on [0.05, 1], expectation by 200-point quadrature (best constant reported as a diagnostic)
chance.facing: unchanged: uniform angle (2*35 + (80-35)) / 360; mutual_facing 1/9 (best constant reported as a diagnostic)
chance.posture: unchanged: best constant answer over the block's facts
chance.locomotion: r1: best constant over {still, moving}; event facts score 0 under it
chance.direction: r1: per sub-kind best constant over the block's present facts, weighted by the sub-kind's share: lateral (labels left_to_right / right_to_left pooled as a mirror pair, away, toward, static), size (approach / same / recede), cam_path (toward / away from camera), updown (up / down)

block_score: unchanged: clip((P - R) / (1 - R), 0, 1) x coverage; P = mean over present facts (presence: balanced accuracy), coverage = present facts / all facts
